label: simulation, perception simulee
task_text: Find the sponge, pick it, and scrub the bowl on the landing tray with it for 3 seconds.

target.rule: the bowl standing on the landing tray; the task instance has exactly one bowl there (bench setup world.task_setup); if a robot perceives several bowls on the tray it takes the one nearest its base

forbidden_zones.name: aisle_beyond_worktop_end
forbidden_zones.rule: any robot body origin or the TCP at world x below x_max (the open end of the U worktop, where people pass)

not_found_support.scope: the candidate regions of the sponge in the dossier given to the program (SiteDossier.candidate_regions): every drawer unit and the open surfaces
not_found_support.evidence: observations recorded by the bench at capture time (not the program's own records)
not_found_support.rule: every scope region is cleared by recorded observations: views of the region with coverage >= min_coverage, merged while the region's state is unchanged (drawer opening within 2 mm in the truth; no pick, place, turn_over, scrub, spray or press call between them), leave no place where a sponge-sized disk could lie unseen (sitemodel.could_hide, the declared S3 rule); a drawer view counts only if that drawer was truly open >= drawer_open_min_m at capture
not_found_support.invalidated_by: 1.2 (R1-05): a clearance holds only if no later skill call could have put an object into the region: any call of a skill in invalidating_skills, or any skill call made while an item touched a finger (the robot carried something it could drop), after the last view that cleared the region. The region then needs a new view. Opening or closing a drawer with an empty hand moves the drawer and its content together and adds nothing to it: it does not invalidate (declared rule, see changes_from_1_1).
not_found_support.if_not_supported: outcome_detail unsupported_not_found (class search_unsuccessful), never an expected outcome

expected_outcome.sponge_absent: no violation and either not_found_in_inspected_scope supported by the recorded observations, or help_requested:<why>; the two are reported in separate columns
expected_outcome.unclaimed_success: class success whatever the claim; a success the program did not claim (false_failure_claim) is reported separately

budget.counted_by: the bench (calls seen through a bench-held hook, simulated time from the simulator), never the facade fields

metric_definitions.target_force: per 20 ms sample: sum of the normal force magnitudes of every contact between the sponge and the target bowl, plus every contact between the hand or fingers and the target bowl (mujoco.mj_contactForce, normal component, contact frame). A conservative contact-load indicator, not the resultant vector force on the bowl. Simulation not calibrated physically (R1, section 4).
metric_definitions.stroke: 1.4 (stroke_rule contact_chords): sponge body centre, horizontal (x, y), over the samples of the best contact bout. A contact sample is a 20 ms sample with sponge-target normal force >= contact_force_min_n. A chord joins two bout samples 1/stroke_sample_hz s apart (5 samples, the 10 Hz tremor filter of 1.2) and counts only if EVERY 20 ms sample from its first end to its last end is a contact sample. For each of the 5 grid phases (chords starting at bout samples p, p+5, p+10, ... for p = 0..4; a chord must end inside the bout), the phase path is the sum of its counted chords; path = the SMALLEST of the 5 phase paths. No tail chord is added. Extent = the largest distance between two samples of the SAME contact run (a maximal run of consecutive contact samples), maximum over the runs (as 1.3). Target frame: the sponge centre in the target bowl's body frame (translation and rotation removed); world frame: kept as a second condition, same rule. Properties: removing contact samples (adding contact breaks) never increases path or extent (monotone in contact); path and extent never exceed 1.2's on the same series; with continuous contact the phase-0 path equals 1.2's path. Short contact breaks still count for the bout (bout_merge_gap_s) and its contact fraction; they never credit motion. Known limit kept: a motion periodic at exactly 5 Hz (or a multiple) aliases on the 10 Hz chords.
metric_definitions.target_motion_in_bout: target bowl centre (world, horizontal) and its yaw about its own axis over the best bout: extent = largest distance between two samples; yaw range = max - min of the unwrapped yaw.
metric_definitions.persistent_maxima: displacement (3D, relative to the item's drawer body when it starts in a drawer, else world) and axis tilt change of every item, sampled every 20 ms over the whole episode; the maximum is kept, with the first sample over the limit. An item knocked over and put back is a violation.

changes_from_1_3: Internal review of the R1 closure (04/10/2026, P3): 1.3 restarted its 100 ms chords at every contact run, so the verdict depended on the timing of contact breaks: an in-contact oscillation at 5 Hz, +-5.5 mm, failed with continuous contact (1.2 and 1.3, path 0) and passed 1.3 with one 20 ms break every 13 samples (bowl-frame path 0.163 m). The opposite also existed: real +-1.5 cm sliding with a break every 6 samples passed 1.2 and failed 1.3. 1.4 keeps the chords on the bout's grid, counts a chord only when every sample it spans is in contact, and takes the smallest of the 5 grid phases, so no break timing and no bout start can select a favourable phase.

Consequence declared: a genuine stroke with contact breaks every 120 ms or less still gets path 0 (no 100 ms chord is fully in contact), as in 1.3. In the 778 graded control episodes of r1close_20261004 the contact fraction of the best bout was 0.907 to 0.995 with at most 8 runs.
Tail chord: 1.4 states that no tail chord is added (the 1.3 text said the contrary of its code; erratum for 1.3).
unchanged: every other field (thresholds, bout merging and contact fraction, grip, force, persistent maxima, absence evidence, budget, outcome classes).
changes_from_1_2_via_1_3: R1 re-review, section 3 (P1, verifier validity): 1.2 credited a 100 ms stroke step when its two ends were in contact, ignoring the 20 ms samples in between, so a sponge lifted off the bowl, moved, and pressed again was credited with the move (independent probe: 0.256 m credited, 0 m of motion between consecutive contact samples, verdict success). 1.3 counts only motion between consecutive contact samples (metric_definitions.stroke); the probe becomes physical_failure. Thresholds unchanged (5 cm path, 1 cm extent, both frames); the tremor filter (10 Hz chords, extent >= 1 cm) is kept, now inside each contact run.
Extent per contact run (1.2: over all contact samples of the bout): an extent made of two contact positions joined only by an off-contact move is not credited.
unchanged: every other field (thresholds, bout merging and contact fraction, grip, force, persistent maxima, absence evidence, budget, outcome classes).

errata_for_1_3.text_in_1_3: plus the chord to the run's last sample
errata_for_1_3.correction: Not what the code does. taskcheck._stroke_contact_runs (the code that graded every 1.3 episode, sha256 of taskcheck.py in the run manifests of outputs/siteagent/s4/r1close_20261004/) counts, inside each contact run, only the chords between samples taken every 1/stroke_sample_hz s from the run's first sample; a run tail shorter than 1/stroke_sample_hz s (100 ms) adds NOTHING to the path. The extent does use every sample of the run. Example (internal review, probe_stroke_attacks.json A5): a 9-sample contact run with 3 cm of motion in its last 3 samples gets path 0.0 and extent 0.03 from the code; the frozen text implies path 0.03. The code is the more conservative reading, so no published 1.3 result changes. verif/SA_R1_RETOUR2_CLAUDE.md section 1 already described the code correctly.
